The LORD showed him the whole land, from Gilead as far as Dan, all of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea (Deuteronomy 34:1-2). That's a view you'd want to take a picture of. Moses gets the full tour from one mountaintop, and I can't even find my own spatula without a search party.

Jericho is right there, because Pisgah faces it, but the LORD shows Moses way more than one city. The text says He showed him the whole land, from Gilead as far as Dan and on down to Zoar (Deuteronomy 34:1-3). That's a lot more than one city. Moses didn't get a peek, friend, he got the full spread.

Egypt isn't on the guest list for this view, friend. The LORD shows Moses the land, from Gilead as far as Dan, and all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea (Deuteronomy 34:1-2). Then He says, "This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob…" (Deuteronomy 34:4). That's what Moses is looking at, a promise, not a way back.

Careful, baker, this one has a twist in the second half. The first part is true. The LORD has let Moses see the land with his own eyes. But then He says, "…but you will not cross into it." (Deuteronomy 34:4) So Moses gets the view, and he doesn't get to walk in.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross into it." (Deuteronomy 34:4) So the seeing is true, and the crossing is the part that's not happening. Moses gets the view, and he doesn't walk in.

Yes, friend. The text says, "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab facing Beth-peor…" (Deuteronomy 34:6). The "He" there is the LORD. Moses is called the servant of the LORD (Deuteronomy 34:5), and the LORD Himself buries him. I think that's tender.

Caleb, one of the men who went to spy out the land (Numbers 13:6), is a good guess because he's a big name in Moses' story. But the passage doesn't name him here. It says, "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab…" (Deuteronomy 34:6). That "He" is the LORD.

Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest (Numbers 20:28), is a fair guess, but the passage doesn't name him here. The text says, "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab facing Beth-peor…" (Deuteronomy 34:6). The "He" is the LORD.

You've got the strength part, but the eyes are the catch. The text says, "…yet his eyes were not weak, and his vitality had not diminished." (Deuteronomy 34:7) So his eyes weren't weak either. At a hundred and twenty, that's a surprise, friend.

That would be a fair guess for most folks at a hundred and twenty, but the text says the opposite. "…yet his eyes were not weak, and his vitality had not diminished." (Deuteronomy 34:7) That little word "yet" tells you it's a surprise. Moses was going strong, friend.

Yes, baker. The Israelites grieved for Moses "…thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end." (Deuteronomy 34:8) That's a whole month of honoring him. When someone matters that much, you take the time.

Seven days is a fair guess, friend. But here the text says the Israelites grieved "…thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end." (Deuteronomy 34:8) So they gave it a lot longer than a week.

Forty is all over Moses' story, so I get why it jumped out. Moses was on the mountain forty days with the LORD (Exodus 24:18). But for the mourning, the text says "…thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end." (Deuteronomy 34:8)

explanations.answer: Moses had laid his hands on him
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The text says Joshua "…was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him." (Deuteronomy 34:9) The reason is right there in the verse. Moses lays on hands, and Joshua steps up filled with wisdom.

explanations.answer: He had fasted alone on the mountain
explanations.explanation: A mountain does show up in this passage, but it's Moses who climbs it (Deuteronomy 34:1). The reason the text gives for Joshua is that "…Moses had laid his hands on him." (Deuteronomy 34:9) Fasting isn't mentioned for Joshua here, friend.

explanations.answer: An angel had appeared to him at night
explanations.explanation: That would make a great scene, but it's not in this passage. The text says Joshua "…was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him." (Deuteronomy 34:9) No angel and no night visit. It's the hands of Moses.

Yes, baker. The text says, "So the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Deuteronomy 34:9) Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him. That's a new leader taking over, and the people listened. I would love a crowd that listens like that when I say the oven is hot.

Doubt would be a normal reaction to a new leader, but the text doesn't say that. It says, "So the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Deuteronomy 34:9) They obeyed Joshua, friend.

No resisting here, baker. The text says, "So the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Deuteronomy 34:9) They obeyed Joshua, son of Nun, the one filled with the spirit of wisdom.

explanations.answer: The LORD knew him face to face
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The text says no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, "…whom the LORD knew face to face…" (Deuteronomy 34:10) That's the closeness the passage holds up. Out of everything Moses did, that's the line that sums him up.

explanations.answer: He never made a single mistake
explanations.explanation: The passage never says that about Moses, and it's not what sets him apart here. It says no prophet has risen like him, "…whom the LORD knew face to face…" (Deuteronomy 34:10) That's the answer, and it's about the LORD knowing him, not about a spotless record.

explanations.answer: He saw every promise come true
explanations.explanation: Think back to the start, friend. The LORD told Moses, "I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross into it." (Deuteronomy 34:4) But that isn't what the passage says sets Moses apart. It says he was the prophet "…whom the LORD knew face to face…" (Deuteronomy 34:10)

That's right, baker. The text says no prophet performed "…all the mighty acts of power and awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel." (Deuteronomy 34:12) The whole nation had a front row seat. That's a send-off worth reading twice.

This one is true, baker. The text says no prophet performed "…all the mighty acts of power and awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel." (Deuteronomy 34:12) Moses did those deeds in the sight of all Israel, so the whole nation saw them.
